blocks.prompt: 5. Discuss domain, range, and graph of the function \(f(x) = 3^{x}\).
blocks.explanation:
Sab se pehle pehchaniye: \(3^{x}\) ek exponential function \(a^{x}\) hai jis ka base \(a = 3\) hai, aur \(3 > 1\).
Diya kya hai? Sirf function \(f(x) = 3^{x}\).
Find kya karna hai? Domain, range, aur graph ki behas (discussion) aur sketch.
Kaunsa rule? Section 1.4.2 ki properties: domain, positive hona, range, intercepts, increasing ya decreasing, one-to-one, aur horizontal asymptote.
Plan: ek ek property likhenge, phir values ka table bana kar graph banayenge, bilkul Example 7 ki tarah.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = 3^{x}\), base \(a = 3\).
Maloom karna: domain, range aur graph.
Tareeqa: \(a > 1\) wale exponential function ki properties (1.4.2) ek ek kar ke lagayenge aur table se points nikaal kar graph banayenge. Imtihan mein "discuss" ka matlab yahi hota hai: har property ka naam, us ka natija, aur ek line ki wajah.

Domain
\[\text{Dom } f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\, = \mathbb{R}\]
Kyun: \(3^{x}\) har real \(x\) ke liye ma'ni rakhta hai: positive, negative, zero, yahan tak ke irrational bhi. Koi value aisi nahin jahan yeh "toot" jaye. Misaal: \(3^{-2} = \frac{1}{9}\), \(3^{0} = 1\), \(3^{1/2} = \sqrt{3}\); har dafa ek pakka number milta hai. Is mein na koi denominator zero hota hai, na kisi negative ka square root.

Positive hona, continuity aur range
\[3^{x} > 0 \text{ for all } x\]
\[x \to \infty:\ 3^{x} \to \infty\]
\[x \to -\infty:\ 3^{x} = \dfrac{1}{3^{-x}} \to 0\]
\[\text{Range } f = \,]0, \infty[\]
Kyun: positive base ki koi bhi power positive hi hoti hai. \(f\) continuous hai (graph mein koi khala nahin), is liye yeh apni do hadon 0 aur \(\infty\) ke darmiyan har value leta hai, magar 0 khud kabhi nahin. Isi liye range ke dono taraf khule brackets hain.

Intercepts
\[f(0) = 3^{0} = 1\]
\(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\); \(x\)-intercept koi nahin.
Kyun: \(y\)-intercept ke liye \(x = 0\) rakha; har base ki zero power 1 hoti hai. \(x\)-intercept ke liye \(3^{x} = 0\) chahiye, jo kabhi nahin hota kyun ke \(3^{x} > 0\). Is liye graph \(x\)-axis ko kabhi nahin kaatta.

Strictly increasing (aur is liye one-to-one)
Agar \(x_{1} < x_{2}\) ho to
\[3^{x_{2}} = 3^{x_{1}} \cdot 3^{x_{2} - x_{1}} > 3^{x_{1}}\]
Kyun: \(x_{2} - x_{1} > 0\) aur base \(3 > 1\), is liye \(3^{x_{2}-x_{1}} > 1\). Kisi number ko 1 se bari cheez se multiply karein to woh barh jata hai. Yani graph baayen se daayen upar charhta hai, aur koi bhi horizontal line ise zyada se zyada ek dafa kaatti hai.

Horizontal asymptote
Jab \(x \to -\infty\), to \(3^{x} \to 0\). Is liye \(y = 0\) (yani \(x\)-axis) horizontal asymptote (woh line jis ke qareeb graph jata hai magar chhoota nahin) hai.
Kyun: baayen taraf curve \(x\)-axis ke jitna chahein qareeb ho jata hai, lekin \(3^{x}\) kabhi zero nahin banta, is liye chhoota nahin.

Values ka table aur graph
\(x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2\) par \(f(x) = \frac{1}{9}, \frac{1}{3}, 1, 3, 9\).
Points lagaiye aur smooth upar charhti curve se joriye (figure dekhiye).
Kyun: har ek qadam daayen jaane par height teen guna ho jati hai: \(1 \to 3 \to 9\). Baayen jaane par teesra hissa: \(1 \to \frac{1}{3} \to \frac{1}{9}\).
Dhyan dein: curve ko \(x\)-axis se milaiye mat; woh sirf qareeb aati hai.

Tasdeeq: answer key bhi Dom \(f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\), Range \(f = \,]0, \infty[\) aur \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hua yahi charhta graph deti hai. Ek aur fori check: \(x = 1\) par graph ki height base ke barabar hoti hai, yani \((1, 3)\); yeh point hamare graph par mojood hai.
blocks.final_answer: Dom \(f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\), Range \(f = \,]0, \infty[\). Graph \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hai, \(x\)-intercept nahin, poora \(x\)-axis ke upar hai, strictly increasing (one-to-one) hai, aur \(x \to -\infty\) par horizontal asymptote \(y = 0\) hai.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of f(x) = 3 to the power x for x from minus 6 to 2. The curve lies above the x-axis, approaches the x-axis on the left (asymptote y = 0), passes through (minus 2, 1/9), (minus 1, 1/3), (0, 1), (1, 3) and (2, 9), and rises steeply to the right.
